newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - April 24.

text.p: THE NATIONAL BUSINESS REVIEW

Casino alchemy: Pile of dirt will be turned to gold: Fill from the Harrah's Sky City casino dumped at a Symonds Street site will soon be transformed into gold as a mixed residential, office and retail development. Page 1.
Qantas poised to take Ansett NZ: Qantas could own Ansett New Zealand by the end of this year. Page 1.
More leaders line up for NBR event: Two more top guns will join Lee Iacocca and Stormin' Norman Schwarzkopf for The National Business Review's World Business leadership event in Auckland. Page 2.
Krukziener seals $40m deal: Ten months after the announcement of the $40 million sale of Auckland's landmark No. 1 Queen Street building, the deal has finally been settled. Page 2.

Publishers appeal defamation case: The Court of Appeal has received from the publishers of the Independent business weekly a notice of a motion to appeal Auckland businessman Andrew Montgomerie's defamation case but a date has yet to be set. Page 2.
Telecom job losses up as restructuring bites: Hundreds of job losses at Telecom appear imminent as restructuring plans announced earlier this month begin to bite. Page 3.

Rugby union seeks player tax review: The Rugby Union has lodged a High Court challenge to Inland Revenue's ruling that top rugby players are employee's of the union, rather than independent and self-employed contractors running their own business activities. Page 3.
Squid industry roars at sealions: Fisheries Minister John Luxton's decision to close the Auckland Islands squid fishery has cost $20 million, quotaholders say. Page 6.

Elder quiet on wine-box deadline leak allegations: Internal Affairs Minister Jack Elder refused to comment on suggestions a mole in the government tipped off Fay Richwhite & Co that the winebox inquiry deadline would be extended. Page 9.

Dunedin mayor states case: Dunedin mayor Sukhi Turner says the decision by Cadbury Confectionery to invest $20 million in capital expenditure over the next two years should hearten local people. Page 9.

New Zealand urged to cash in on lucrative teaching market: English language teaching is a growth industry New Zealand should continue to cash in on, the director general of the British Council advised during a visit to Auckland. Page 10.

Distillers claim home stills cost tax and lives: Home distilling of spirits is potentially dangerous and is costing the government up to $37 million a year in lost excise and GST, and industry lobby claimed on Wednesday. Page 11.
US firm buys stake in 'new' Spicers: A private US investment firm, Sterling Grace, has displayed a show of confidence in New Zealand's struggling financial services industry. Page 12.
Manufacturers up pressure to ease Tasman trade rules: Manfed is maintaining pressure on the government to persuade Australia to free up the rules of origin governing transtasman trade. Page 12.

Exporters face tougher time in Southeast Asia: New Zealand exporters of fish, some processed foods, timber and forest products to Southeast Asia will face increasing competition from local suppliers around the turn of the century, according to a Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade study. Page 14.
Auckland Airport for sale -- again?: British Airport Authority and the giant US Lockheed Corporation are still interested in buying a stake in Auckland International Airport. Page 1.
Countrywide's profit leaps: Countrywide Bank's after-tax profit leapt 30 percent to $54 million in the 28 February year, compared with $42 million in the previous year. Page 2.
Lion seeks salvation in Stella: Lion Breweries is reputedly negotiating with Stella Artois' owners to launch a locally brewed version of the Belgian lager in New Zealand. Page 3.

Kiwi Packaging plucks $1m from Fortex ruins: Fortex receiver Alan Isaac was last week ordered to pay almost $1 million to Kiwi Packaging Ltd -- the company providing the boxing for its meat products when Fortex went into receivership on 23 March 1994. Page 3.
Planners' land squeeze blights industry, fuels inflation: The Christchurch City Council is doubling the amount of residential zoned land in a draft city plan covering the next 20 years. Page 4.
Wellington entrenpreneur Lloyd Morrison should know next week if his Australian investment vehicle, Infratil Australia, has won a slice of Australia's A$3 billion airport privatisation. Page 6.
